channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: Skadden hires another partner from Latham
item.description: Samuel Pape has left Latham & Watkins for Skadden Arps Slate Meagher & Flom in London, weeks after Sophie Lamb KC made the same move.

item.title: UK court to assess India’s challenge to Gibson Dunn in Devas dispute
item.description: A London court has ruled in India’s favour on preliminary issues in a dispute over whether Gibson Dunn has the authority to represent three Mauritian entities in an investment treaty claim.

item.title: Canada faces ICSID claim over Russia sanctions
item.description: A billionaire who renounced his Russian citizenship has made good on his threat to bring an ICSID claim worth at least US$250 million against Canada over its refusal to take him off its sanctions list.

item.title: Abu Dhabi fund wins claim over collapse of Austrian property empire
item.description: UPDATED WITH TRIBUNAL: Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala has reportedly won a €700 million ICC award against affiliates of Austria’s troubled Signa property group.

item.title: OHLA pursues Pemex over project payments
item.description: A subsidiary of Spanish construction group OHLA has brought a US action against Mexico’s national oil and gas company Pemex to enforce a US$15 million ICC award arising from a contract for work on a hydrogen plant and natural gas pipeline.

item.title: Canadian silk joins Fasken as senior counsel
item.description: Timothy Ellam KC has retired from the partnership at Canadian firm McCarthy Tétrault, where he was co-head of the international arbitration practice, to join Fasken as senior counsel.

item.title: Brazil’s appeal in Petrobras shareholder feud clears hurdle in Paris
item.description: A Paris court has found that Brazil can proceed with an appeal of an order enforcing an annulled partial award in a US$41 billion arbitration brought by two minority shareholders in state-run oil company Petrobras.

item.title: Gharavi will not preside over reopened Jordan Chiles case
item.description: Hamid Gharavi has said he will not continue to preside over the Jordan Chiles case for the Court of Arbitration of Sport after a Swiss court dismissed conflict of interest allegations against him on multiple grounds and reopened the merits of the case based on new evidence that emerged after the award.

item.title: Webuild brings new ICSID claim against Argentina
item.description: Italy’s Webuild has filed a new ICSID claim worth more than US$150 million against Argentina over a highway concession – as the state applies to annul an award requiring it to pay damages to the construction group over a separate project.

item.title: Port operator brings ICC claim against Panama
item.description: A subsidiary of Hong Kong-based conglomerate CK Hutchison has filed a US$2 billion ICC claim against Panama, accusing the state of attempting to seize a coveted port concession at the Panama Canal.
